Negative estimates retained as signed estimates, not claimed negative true variances. Full received-universe leave-own-out mean return market; only close.

what_the_new_estimator_changes: Changes overlapping120-observation rolling beta histories into six non-overlapping21-observation slope estimates.
Removes market/stock variance normalization and subtracts a mean sampling-variance estimate.
Uses signed excess variance and negative direction instead of low normalized raw beta-history variance.
why_this_is_not_an_independent_economic_: Both scores prefer stocks whose market exposure changes less through time, using the same stock/market close-return history. SamplingSE is estimation uncertainty derived from the same regressions. Correcting measurement noise is a statistically meaningful estimator change, but it does not by itself establish a new economic information mechanism or satisfy the existing RR02 reopening condition. Merely stating a new window/partition/normalization cannot erase the already observed mechanism failure.
measurement_risks_if_a_later_explicit_re: Classical OLS samplingSE squared is conditional on residual/serial dependence assumptions; it is not automatically the true estimation noise under heteroskedastic or autocorrelated stock returns.

A strongly negative excess_between can favor stocks with high residual noise or unstable variance estimates. It must not be narrated as confirmed exceptionally stable exposure or a negative true variance.
Noise subtraction may change ranking materially, but that must be distinguished from the already closed residual-risk/volatility mechanisms before any return test.
A label-free source/estimator validation demonstrating a specific measurement fault in the old RR02 may motivate a separately recorded reopen; the new formula alone does not establish that fault.
Six small samples must each be paired, full rank and sufficiently supported; missingness/singular fits cannot be filled or truncated after outcomes.
